claim: The group filter runs inside the memory search so out-of-scope records never take up the result limit; a set with no memory_groups reads untagged only.
source_excerpt: The filter runs inside the memory search, so records outside a request's groups never take up the search's result limit.
verify_hint: Check _scope_filter use in src/sqllens/agent/integrations/chromadb/agent_memory.py where= passed to collection.query
evidence: agent_memory.py:267-280 (search_similar_usage) and 464-472 (search_text_memories) compute _scope_filter() before the executor and pass it, ANDed via and_filters, as where= to collection.query with n_results=limit, so filtering happens inside the Chroma query and out-of-scope rows cannot consume the limit. _memory_groups.py:54-63 scope_filter([]) returns {memory_tagged: {$ne: True}} (untagged only); non-empty adds $or of untagged and $contains per group. factory.py:88-97,173 wires group_scope only when rule_sets is set; with no selection scope is () = untagged only. No-rule-set-file case (filter None, reads everything) is explicitly stated in docs rule-sets.md:247, so the doc matches. Hostile input considered: request with a set lacking memory_groups, or no selection -> untagged filter, traced OK.

claim: verify-memory under --rule-set S reads exactly what a query_database request under S reads.
source_excerpt: `sqllens verify-memory` under `--rule-set S` reads exactly what a `query_database` request under `S` reads.
verify_against: verify-memory agent construction and RuleSetSelection publishing
verify_hint: Check how cli.py verify_memory publishes the RuleSetSelection and builds the agent via build_agent with group_scope
evidence: cli.py:665-671 passes --rule-set/--user/--account to run_verification. eval/runner.py:214,224,275 builds metadata under the file's metadata keys and validates it with select_rule_set. The production driver (runner.py:281-288) calls query_database_impl_with_widgets(metadata=..., agent=verify_agent), the same entry point query_database uses. That entry runs select_rule_set and set_rule_set_selection(selection) (tools/query_database.py:706,757), so the RuleSetSelection is published exactly as for a live request. The verify agent comes from build_agent(forced_cfg, allow_memory_writes=False) (runner.py:281). In factory.py:173 its ChromaAgentMemory gets group_scope=_rule_set_memory_scope(rule_sets), which reads current_rule_set_selection() and returns rule_sets.memory_groups_for(selection.name) (factory.py:88-97). That is the same scope function a served agent gets. allow_memory_writes only affects track_usage (counter updates), not the read filter. verification_config (runner.py:80-108) leaves cfg.rule_sets unchanged. It changes save flags, show_details and caps, and resolves similarity_threshold through the same default-profile path query_database uses; none of these alter which groups are readable. Absolute-claim input traced: a request under S with S's memory_groups gets the same scope tuple in both paths. Dispatch-time dependency: the group filter is applied by the same memory object construction in both.

claim: _scope_filter calls group_scope() on the caller's event loop before run_in_executor because the executor thread does not see the context var.
source_excerpt: It must run before `run_in_executor`, which does not copy context variables: on the worker thread `current_rule_set_selection()` is `None`.
verify_against: ChromaAgentMemory search methods and asyncio loop.run_in_executor
verify_hint: Check ordering of _scope_filter vs run_in_executor in search_similar_usage and search_text_memories in agent_memory.py
evidence: In agent_memory.py, search_similar_usage (line 267) and search_text_memories (line 464) call self._scope_filter() in the async method body, before the inner _search closure is passed to run_in_executor (lines 355, 504). _scope_filter (138-143) calls self._group_scope() on the caller's task. The closure only captures the precomputed group_filter, so the worker thread never reads the context var. This matches the claim. asyncio's loop.run_in_executor does not propagate contextvars (unlike asyncio.to_thread), so the stated reason is correct.

When no rule-set file is configured group_scope is None, which is outside the claim's rule-set context.

Write paths: agent_memory.py:246 and :443 spread **group_metadata(groups) (save_tool_usage / save_text_memory), reached from store.py add_sql_pair (183-194, groups=groups) and add_schema_doc (196-197). store.py set_groups (229-257) strips both GROUPS_KEY and TAGGED_KEY from existing metadata then merges group_metadata(updates[id]), so both keys are set together; comment at 254-255 notes Chroma merges on update. claim: The group scope is read on the event loop before run_in_executor because the executor does not copy context variables
source_excerpt:
# Must run before run_in_executor: the executor does not copy context
        # variables, so a scope read on the worker thread sees no request.
verify_against: agent_memory.py search_similar_usage and search_text_memories, and rule_sets.current_rule_set_selection contextvar
verify_hint: Check that every search method that applies group scope calls self._scope_filter() outside the _search closure, including any other search path (e.g. get_recent_memories) used for the system-prompt context
evidence: agent_memory.py:138-143 _scope_filter reads self._group_scope() (the contextvar-backed callable) synchronously. search_similar_usage calls it at line 267 and search_text_memories at line 464, both before defining the _search closure and before awaiting run_in_executor (lines 355, 504). The closures only use the precomputed group_filter (e.g. line 469 and_filters). Wrapped loop.run_in_executor does not propagate contextvars (unlike asyncio.to_thread), so the comment is accurate. Absolute-claim input considered: a search path reading scope inside the worker closure; none exists. get_recent_memories (357-403) and get_recent_text_memories (506) do not apply group scope at all, so they do not read it on a worker thread; their only caller of note, default.py:545/552, is the /memories display command, not the search paths the claim names. Whether those should be scoped is outside this claim.

claim: sqllens._memory_groups exports GROUPS_KEY, TAGGED_KEY, group_metadata and record_groups; record_groups(metadata) returns the record's groups (empty for an untagged or legacy record without the keys), and group_metadata(groups) returns metadata setting both GROUPS_KEY and TAGGED_KEY.
verify_hint: Check `record_groups` and `group_metadata` in `_memory_groups.py`
evidence: src/sqllens/_memory_groups.py defines GROUPS_KEY (l.15), TAGGED_KEY (l.20), group_metadata (l.30-39) and record_groups (l.42-51). record_groups returns [] when TAGGED_KEY is not True (l.44-45), so a legacy or untagged record without the keys yields []. group_metadata returns {GROUPS_KEY: names, TAGGED_KEY: True} for any non-empty groups (l.39). Scope note: for empty or None groups it returns {} by design (l.37-38, documented: ChromaDB refuses empty lists), so 'sets both' applies to a tagged (non-empty) group set. That is the intended meaning of the claim.

claim: set_groups relies on Chroma's collection.update merging metadata, so writing group_metadata for every updated record overwrites both group keys; with an empty groups value, a stale key would survive.
verify_against: chromadb Collection.update in the installed chromadb package; src/sqllens/_memory_groups.py group_metadata
verify_hint: Check `Collection.update` metadata semantics and what `group_metadata` returns for each groups input that set_groups receives from the importer
evidence: Chroma's SqliteMetadataSegment._update_metadata (chromadb site-packages in repo .venv, segment/impl/metadata/sqlite.py:310-325) deletes only keys whose value is None, then inserts the given keys, so update merges and omitted keys survive. group_metadata (_memory_groups.py:30-39) returns {} for empty groups and {GROUPS_KEY: names, TAGGED_KEY: True} otherwise, so for non-empty groups both keys are overwritten and for empty groups a stale key would survive. set_groups (store.py:229-257) writes group_metadata for each record and its comment says as much. The importer's plan.updates (importer.py:156-160) holds only records whose merged group set strictly grew (union with incoming), so the groups are never empty. The claim holds as described.

claim: dedup_entries covers the rows iter_all turns into bundle items and raises MemoryCorruptionError when iter_all would.
source_excerpt:
Covers the rows :meth:`iter_all` turns into bundle items and raises
        :class:`MemoryCorruptionError` when it does; call it on the memory worker.
verify_hint: Compare the row filters in `dedup_entries` (content strip, args_json parse, question type) with `_bundle_from_metadatas`; e.g. a whitespace-only content doc or a pair with non-string question
evidence: store.py:207 dedup_entries calls self._bundle_from_metadatas on the same collection.get metadatas that iter_all (store.py:285-286) uses, so the MemoryCorruptionError wholesale-skip check (store.py:329-343) is identical. Coverage: every row iter_all turns into an item is a dict-metadata row that is either is_text_memory with a non-blank str content (SchemaDoc _require_non_blank, schema.py:119-122) or a run_sql row with str non-blank sql and str non-blank question (schema.py:85-93); dedup_entries (store.py:212-226) includes all of these (content str and strip non-empty; sql str non-empty; question str). Whitespace-only content is rejected by SchemaDoc and also excluded by dedup; non-string question fails SqlPair and is excluded by dedup. dedup_entries is a superset only in that it also keeps rows violating length limits or whitespace-only sql/blank question; that does not break 'covers'.

claim: Invalid memory_groups (empty, duplicate, non-string, empty string) raise RuleSetFileError whose message contains 'memory_groups'.

evidence: RuleSet.memory_groups (rule_sets.py:394) is list[NonEmptyStr]|None with min_length=1 (empty list), NonEmptyStr=StrictStr min_length=1 (non-string, empty string; line 58), and _unique_memory_groups calls _no_duplicates (lines 396-401, raises ValueError 'duplicate memory group'). load_rule_sets catches ValidationError (848-850) and formats each error via _validation_problems/_record_path (796-811) which prefixes the loc, e.g. 'rule_sets[0].memory_groups[1]: ...'.
